title: Using CTT for Comprehensive Superfamily Gene Annotations
author: Zhihua Hua
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zf4f3qw

steps.title: Clone the CTT package
steps.instruction: Clone the CTT package from GitHub into the home directory.

steps.title: Compile dependencies
steps.instruction: Compile the required software packages. Note that an admin (sudo) user account is required for the genewise program.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to the dependencies directory: cd ./ctt/dependencies/
Run: make all to compile blast, hmmer, CD-HIT, genewise, pfam database, and pfamscan

steps.title: Activate WISECONFIGDIR
steps.instruction: Activate the WISECONFIGDIR path to allow genewise to recognize its configuration.

substeps.instruction: Logout and login to the server once.

steps.title: Retrieve species databases
steps.instruction: Download the genome sequence, protein sequence, and gene annotation GFF3 files for the target species from the Ensembl website (https://useast.ensembl.org/index.html) into the './ctt/species_databases' directory.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to 'Downloads' -> 'Download databases' on the Ensembl website.
Use wget to download the complete genome file (e.g., wget -r -nd -A '*dna.toplevel.fa.gz' ftp://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-95/fasta/homo_sapiens/dna/).

Use wget to download the complete set of protein sequences (e.g., wget -r -nd -A '*.fa.gz' ftp://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-95/fasta/homo_sapiens/pep/), removing ab initio annotation files if present.
Use wget to download the complete GFF3 file (e.g., wget -r -nd -A '*.gff3.gz' ftp://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-95/gff3/homo_sapiens), removing single chromosome annotation files.

steps.title: Organize database files
steps.instruction: Create a tab-delimited file named 'organismal_genome_gff3_proteome_files.tab' in the './ctt/species_databases/' directory containing the file names for the genome sequence, GFF3, and protein sequence for each organism.

substeps.instruction: Organize the file names in Excel and save as a text file, or use the vim editor to create the file directly in the directory.

steps.title: Create BLAST databases
steps.instruction: Generate BLAST databases for tBLASTn and BLASTp searches within the './ctt/species_databases' directory.

substeps.instruction: For tBLASTn (nucleotide): run makeblastdb -in genome_file_name -dbtype nucl -out genome_file_name.db
For BLASTp (protein): run makeblastdb -in proteome_file_name -dbtype prot -out proteome_file_name.db

steps.title: Download superfamily seed sequences
steps.instruction: Obtain the seed sequence file for the superfamily of interest from the Pfam website (http://pfam.xfam.org).

substeps.instruction: Search for the superfamily name or ID in the 'JUMP TO' search engine.
Under 'Format an alignment', select: 'seed' alignment, 'Fasta' format, 'Alphabetical' order, 'All upper case' sequences, and 'No gaps (unaligned)'.
Click 'Generate' to download the file (formatted as '(PfamID)_seed.txt').
Transfer the file to the './ctt/seeds/' directory.

steps.title: Run CTT annotation
steps.instruction: Execute the CTT annotation script from the './ctt/' directory using the following command format: perl ctt.pl -seed family_seed_file.txt -f Pfam_family_name -superfamily simplified_family_id_you_named
